title: Puppy Biting: Why It Happens And How To Stop It
description:
Puppy biting is normal, painful and fixable. Here is why it happens and the gentle way to stop it.

script: Puppy biting is normal, painful, and fixable. Puppies explore the world with their mouths, and they are also teething between about three and six months old, which makes chewing feel good. They also learn bite control from playing with littermates, and when a puppy bites too hard, the other puppy yelps and stops the game. You can do the same. When your puppy's teeth touch your skin, say ow in a calm voice and pause play for a few seconds. If your puppy calms down, resume. If the biting continues, step away for a short time out. Then offer a chew toy the moment they open their mouth for you, so they learn what is okay to chew. Keep a few safe toys in every room, and try freezing a wet washcloth for sore gums. Avoid rough hand wrestling, which teaches your puppy that hands are toys. Tired puppies bite more, so make sure they get regular naps. Stay patient and consistent, because most puppies bite much less by five or six months. If biting seems aggressive, ask a trainer for help.
